title: Data Sensitivity Sorter for AI Tools
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Judgment activity in which learners decide which class of AI tool each of eight items of research data may be given to under a four-class illustrative data classification: Class 0 Public, Class 1 Internal, Class 2 Unpublished, and Class 3 Obligated. Each item has one attempt in a fixed order with feedback naming the item's class and the reason. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and the eight items grouped by class.

educational.topic: Classifying research data before giving it to AI tools
learningObjectives: Judge which class of AI tool an item of research data may be given to under a four-class illustrative policy, for eight items, with at least 7 of 8 correct
Recognize unpublished results, vendor files under NDA, and participants' personal data as restricted even when they are not secret
prerequisites: Privacy, confidential data, unpublished results, and data governance from the section Privacy, Confidentiality, and Governance of Chapter 18
The four data classes of the illustrative classification in Table 1 of Chapter 18

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; the tool-class list and buttons are native HTML controls reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check-mark or X symbols as well as color, and the item's class is marked with an arrow and the words (this item) as well as an outline; the color pair is the color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito blue and vermillion; the base text size is chosen per width from 18 px down to 14 px (13 px only below about 340 px wide) so that every state fits.

controls.label: Choose a tool class...
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the four tool classes: Any tool; Approved hosted tool or local; Local model, or hosted with the advisor's approval; Local model only, if the agreement allows. Disabled after the answer is submitted.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the chosen tool class for the current item (one attempt per item). Enabled once a tool class is chosen.

controls.label: Next Item / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after the answer is submitted. Advances to the next item, and after item 8 shows the score, the mastery statement, and the items grouped by class.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Four-way judgment of concrete research data against a stated classification, with one attempt per item, immediate feedback naming the class, and a summary grouping the items by class
keyQuestions: Is the item public, internal, unpublished, or under an obligation such as an NDA, a license, export control, or participant consent?
If the item falls in two classes, which is the more restrictive one?
commonMisconceptions: Unpublished results are fine to share if they are not under an NDA
If a file is on a shared drive it may be given to any tool
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 items answered with the answer-key tool class on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the classification table is exploration and is not evidence of mastery
